walkthroughs.body_html:
Stars — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Stars brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Stars.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the spectral class of the Sun?
options: O
A
G
M

mcqs.q: Which class of stars is hottest?
options: O
G
K
M

mcqs.q: Why are Type Ia supernovae used as 'standard candles'?
options: Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
They have nearly uniform peak brightness, so their apparent brightness reveals distance.
Because they happen at regular time intervals.
It moves backwards.

mcqs.q: Why was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
options: It moves backwards.
It is too small to be a planet.
It does not clear its orbital neighbourhood of similar-sized bodies.
It is made of fire.

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: It is made of fire.
It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.
Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
